votes.reasoning: The second perl pattern in check-source-ratchets.sh rejects the point-free `Int.init` unless a labeled initializer follows it. In a scratch FooWireTypes.swift, `.map(Int.init)` was flagged (exit 1), while `Int(saturating:)` and `Int64.init(exactly:)` passed. The HEAD bare-int regex finds 0 hits on `.map(Int.init)`, so the reversal fails as expected. Self-test [3/4] covers this. A missing directory fails closed through pipefail on find (self-test [4/4]).

The bare-Int check moved into the shared script and gained a second alternative that rejects point-free `.init` unless it has a label (check-source-ratchets.sh:105). The self-test pins it both ways: [3/4] must reject 7 forms, and [2/4] must accept the labeled `Int.init(saturating:)` and `radix:`. The `} continue { close ARGV if eof;` idiom is a known perl trick that resets $. for each file, so line numbers stay per-file. It is terse but correct. No duplication remains, since the old grep in validate.sh was removed.

The bare-Int ratchet moved from validate.sh into check-source-ratchets.sh:94-110, which adds the point-free Int.init form. The committed self-test plants that form. The WIRE_TYPES_DIR knob is kept and no other file used it. CI now runs this check too (ci.yml:45-46), so the lockstep with validate.sh is closed. The docs at CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md:550-551 are updated.
